h1: The 7 Best Electric Griddles Under $100 for Pancakes, Eggs and Family Breakfasts, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 electric griddles under $100, scored on cooking surface, temperature range, grease control, coating and cleanup.
summary: The Presto 07061 22-inch ceramic griddle is the best electric griddle under $100 for families, with a big PFAS-free ceramic plate and removable handles. The Chefman XL 10 by 20 is the value pick with a 200 to 420F range, and the bella adds a warming tray.
intro: Most buyers pick a griddle by surface area and then discover the real differences in how it handles grease and heat. A flat plate with no drip path lets bacon fat pool at the edges. A control you cannot remove means the whole unit stays out of the sink. Those details decide whether a griddle becomes a weekend habit or a cupboard resident.

Seven griddles are ranked, all at or under $100. Scoring covers surface size, temperature range, grease management, coating and how easy cleanup is. Every figure is from a listing, and unlisted wattage or warranty is noted as missing.

products.name: Presto 07061 22-Inch Electric Ceramic Griddle
products.verdict: A 22 inch plate with a PFAS-free ceramic coating, textured nonstick and removable handles.
products.description:
The Presto 07061 has a 22 inch plate with a PFAS-free ceramic coating, a textured nonstick surface and removable handles. It costs under $100.

It wins on space and coating. A 22 inch plate fits a full family breakfast in one go, and a ceramic surface avoids the fluorinated chemicals some shoppers want to skip. Removable handles let it slide into a cupboard. The cost is storage space and no listed temperature range.

Buy it if you cook for four or more. Skip it if you have a tiny kitchen.
products.idealFor: Family breakfasts for four or more.

products.name: Chefman XL Electric Griddle, 10 by 20 Inch
products.verdict: Roomy cooking area, heat up to 420F and a body you can wash in the sink.
products.description:
The Chefman XL offers a 10 by 20 inch cooking area, heat from 200 to 420F, a control that pops off, a body safe to submerge and a drip tray. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

An immersible body is the standout at this price: with the control removed you can wash the whole griddle in the sink. The 420F ceiling is enough for a good sear on pancakes and burgers. It ranks second because the listing does not name the coating.

Buy it if you want washability on a budget. Skip it if you care about coating type.
products.skipIf: You want a named ceramic coating.

products.name: bella 10 x 20 Inch Electric Griddle with Warming Tray
products.verdict: A ceramic nonstick 10 by 20 inch plate with a removable probe, a warming tray and room for 10 eggs.
products.description:
The bella has a 10 by 20 inch ceramic nonstick surface, a removable temperature probe, a warming tray and room for 10 eggs. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

The warming tray keeps the first pancakes hot while the last ones cook, which matters at a table of hungry people. It ranks third because the listing gives no temperature range.

Buy it if you cook batches and serve together. Skip it if you want a stated range.

products.name: Amazon Basics Electric Griddle with Ceramic Coating
products.verdict: A detachable, dishwasher-safe plate with grease channels and a 200 to 400F range.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics griddle has a ceramic coating, a 200 to 400F range, a removable probe, a detachable dishwasher-safe plate and grease channels with a drip tray. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

A dishwasher-safe plate is the easiest cleanup here. It ranks fourth because 400F is the lowest ceiling in the group and no plate size is listed.

Buy it if you want the dishwasher to do the work. Skip it if you want higher heat.

products.name: Presto 07046 Tilt 'n Drain Big Griddle
products.verdict: A tilt-and-drain design that holds 12 slices of French toast and has a cool-touch exterior.
products.description:
The Presto 07046 has a tilt-and-drain design that can sit level or tilted, holds 12 slices of French toast and has a cool-touch exterior. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

Tilting sends grease to one side so bacon and sausage drain without a drip tray. It ranks fifth because the listing names no coating and no range.

Buy it if you cook greasy foods often. Skip it if you want listed coating details.

products.name: Presto 07047 16-Inch Cool Touch Electric Griddle
products.verdict: A 10.5 by 16 inch surface with a cool-touch base, a backstop ledge and PFAS-free ceramic nonstick.
products.description:
The Presto 07047 has a 10.5 by 16 inch surface, a cool-touch base, a backstop ledge and a PFAS-free ceramic nonstick coating. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

The backstop ledge keeps pancake batter and eggs from sliding off the back. It ranks sixth because the surface is smaller than the leaders and no temperature range is listed.

Buy it if you cook for two. Skip it if you feed a crowd.

products.name: Chefman Electric Griddle, 9.8 by 15.7 Inch
products.verdict: A 9.8 by 15.7 inch flat top with a 200 to 420F range, removable control and drip tray.
products.description:
This Chefman has a 9.8 by 15.7 inch surface, a 200 to 420F range, a removable control, an immersible flat top and a drip tray. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

It is the compact version of the XL, with the same washability. It ranks last because the XL gives far more cooking area for similar money.

Buy it if space is tight. Skip it if the XL fits.

whatMatters.detail: A 10 by 20 inch plate fits about eight pancakes, while 22 inches handles a family batch. Choose by the largest meal you cook, and check storage space.
Pancakes cook around 350F and searing wants 400F or more. A 200 to 420F range covers both. Listings without a range give less control.
Drip trays and grease channels keep fat off the counter. A tilt-and-drain design sends it to one side. Look for one of these if you cook bacon.
Ceramic coatings avoid fluorinated chemicals but can wear sooner than good nonstick. Use silicone or wooden utensils and avoid high heat for long.
A removable control lets you immerse the body. A detachable plate can go in the dishwasher. Either removes the awkward wipe-down.

faq.q: Is ceramic coating as good as nonstick?
faq.a: It is PFAS-free and works well when new, but it can wear faster. Use soft utensils and moderate heat.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a griddle?
faq.a: Ignoring storage. A 22 inch plate takes real cupboard room. Measure before you buy.

faq.q: Is the Presto 22 inch worth it over the Chefman XL?
faq.a: For a family, yes, for the extra area and ceramic coating. For two or three people, the Chefman is cheaper and washes easily.

faq.q: How hot should I run it?
faq.a: About 350F for pancakes and 375 to 400F for bacon and burgers. Preheat until the light signals ready.
Let it cool, then wipe or, if the control is removable and the body immersible, wash it in the sink. Never immerse the control.
Avoid them on ceramic or nonstick surfaces. Use silicone or wood.

finalTake: The Presto 07061 22-inch ceramic griddle is the best electric griddle under $100 for families, with a big PFAS-free plate. The Chefman XL is the washable value pick, and the bella adds a warming tray. Measure your storage and decide between area and easy cleanup.
